The FOMC statement’s tone is modestly positive (strong labor market, moderate growth), but SLOOS signals temper this. Banks reported weaker C&I loan demand (notably at foreign banks serving middle‑market firms) and weaker demand in construction and land development loans, while demand in nonfarm nonresidential and multifamily CRE was unchanged. Lenders cited the economic outlook and liquidity as reasons for tightening, with some easing attributable to competition. These credit indicators reinforce the statement’s concerns around weak business investment and justify a slightly more cautious stance than the baseline.
